visual: Compact, densely branched dwarf deciduous shrub with small rounded purplish-red to deep burgundy leaves, becoming brighter crimson-red in autumn; small pale yellow spring flowers are followed by glossy red berries.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate moderately dry conditions.
soilWarning: No waterlogging; shade dulls the foliage
prune: Little pruning required; remove damaged or unwanted stems after flowering and trim low hedges as necessary.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten; thorny stems can cause injury and gloves are recommended when handling.
resilience: Exceptionally cold hardy and tolerant of exposure, varied soils and periods of dryness once established.
uses: Low hedging, border edging, containers, rock gardens, colour contrast and low-maintenance shrub planting.

visual: Slow-growing evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy finely serrated dark green leaves and autumn to winter flowers ranging from white and pale pink to deep rose-pink; many cultivated forms are lightly fragrant.
water: Keep evenly moist, particularly during summer when the following season's flower buds are forming; rainwater is preferable in hard-water areas.
soilWarning: No lime; shelter from cold winds and drought
prune: Requires little pruning; lightly shape after flowering where necessary.
resilience: Hardy through much of the UK in a sheltered position, though flowers and buds can be damaged by severe frost and cold winds.
uses: Autumn colour, woodland gardens, sheltered borders, containers, courtyards and wall-side planting.
uncertain: The label phrases 'Les Camélias d’Automne' and 'floraison automne' describe autumn-flowering Camellia sasanqua rather than identifying a specific cultivar.

visual: Compact spreading deciduous shrub with slender lance-shaped green leaves that develop vivid red autumn colour, contrasting with clusters of intensely rich blue plumbago-like flowers in late summer and autumn.
water: Water regularly while establishing; thereafter keep moderately moist but well drained.
soilWarning: No waterlogging; sun for flower and colour
prune: Prune in spring, cutting back old flowering growth to encourage vigorous new shoots.
resilience: Hardy through most of the UK and tolerant of exposed conditions provided the soil drains adequately.
uses: Border fronts, cottage gardens, gravel gardens, containers, wall-side planting and late-season colour.
